subject: MAP: Performance evaluation runbook + multi-region failover measurements
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: sre-team@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - performance scope

Thanks for the kickoff call earlier. Per our side, we want the MAP to cover:
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) for normal and burst traffic
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for prompt+tool calls
- Sustained throughput at 1k/5k/10k concurrent tokens/sec equivalents
- Concurrency scaling profile (1, 8, 32, 128 sessions)
- Multi-region probe (us-east, eu-west, apac-sin) including failover times

We need an acceptance threshold for launch: p95 < 250ms (in-region) and failover < 6s for single-region outage. Can Redwood propose concrete test scripts and a data collection plan?

Alex
Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
From: priyom.das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: alex.morgan@acme.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - performance scope

Alex — appreciated the clear targets. Attaching an initial MAP workbook (MAP-v2.xlsx) and a short runbook for the benchmark harness. High level plan:

1) Test plan and roles (week of Jul 20)
   - Redwood SRE (Jonas) will provision test pools in us-east, eu-west, apac-sin
   - Acme SRE will provide 3 steady-state traffic profiles and a list of representative prompt templates
2) Synthetic runs (Jul 22–24)
   - TTFT probe (10k quick probes per region), cold vs warm cache
   - Concurrency sweep (1/8/32/128 sessions) to build throughput curves
3) Failover simulation (Jul 26)
   - Region pull: simulate region outage and measure routing/failover times for production pins
4) Data collection and analysis (Jul 27–30)
   - P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, tail latencies, KV cache hit rates, model variant breakdown
5) Results review and acceptance decision (Aug 3)

I've included example script snippets in benchmark-scripts.tar.gz and a sample metrics schema. Would you be able to confirm the prompt templates and a test API key with limited quota by Tue (Jul 20)?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: jonas.weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: alex.morgan@acme.com; priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation runbook + multi-region failover measurements

Alex / Priyom — quick status update from infra side: test pools are up in the three regions (g4dn equivalent in us, g5-like in eu, and t4g in apac for a representative lower-tier). Notes:
- We're deploying two model variants: base-float32 and q4_8bit. Please expect ~1.6x throughput difference in quantized runs.
- KV cache warm/cold is simulated by running a 30-minute prefix load before the window for warm runs.
- Synthetic probe runner will stamp each event with request-id/hubspot-deal and upload metrics to the shared Drive folder.

Planned smoke runs Wed morning then the full concurrency sweep Thu. Flagging that the apac pool currently has slightly higher p95 due to network egress—we'll try an alternate peering if Acme can accept a short test outage window.

Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: sre-team@acme.com
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation runbook + multi-region failover measurements

Thanks Jonas — go ahead with the peering test for apac; Acme SRE will standby Thursday 18:00-20:00 UTC for a maintenance window. Also clarifying acceptance: the p95 target is for in-region traffic to the pinned model variant; fallback to quantized variant acceptable in catastrophic overload but must be measured and documented.

Alex
From: priyom.das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: alex.morgan@acme.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP: Performance evaluation runbook + multi-region failover measurements

On Tue, Jul 28, 2026 at 08:34 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick status: smoke runs completed. Initial numbers look promising but we have a couple of anomalies to examine before the final report.

Update and asks:
- Please review the attached metrics schema and add any additional fields Acme needs for compliance.
- If procurement expects any contract-level SLA exceptions (failover < 6s), let us know — we'll route to contract team.
- We're planning the results review call Aug 3 at 14:00 UTC. Is that workable?

Separately, I'm attaching the early results CSV (results-summary-20260804.csv) for transparency; note the apac p95 spike during the peering test. We'll annotate root cause.

Best,
Priyom
From: procurement@acme.com <procurement@acme.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.morgan@acme.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 16:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation runbook + multi-region failover measurements

Thanks for the deck and the CSV. Procurement is tracking the MAP milestones against the PO timeline. A couple items before we can finalize:
- We need the documented test acceptance criteria in the MAP workbook (explicit pass/fail per metric).
- Please confirm whether the agreed failover < 6s is only for active routing (DNS + routing policy) or also includes model spin-up time for a cold instance.
- If Acme agrees to the fallback quantized-variant behavior, procurement will permit the contingency clause in the PO, otherwise we need a credit schedule for missed SLOs.

Can the Redwood commercial team provide a one-page summary of final acceptance and any proposed credit language by Tue Aug 10?

Regards,
Acme Procurement
